$comment: The interaction inventory (editor ADR 1202): the spec-derived sections are written by `bun scripts/interaction-inventory.mjs --sync`; the tests' gates, fixture, layers and requirements, the interactions, the exceptions and enforcedGates are curated. The guard: `bun scripts/interaction-inventory.mjs`.

fixtures.description: simple page with two overlapping rectangles and a locked third object
group containing path and text frame
linked text frames and IME test text
20-page IDML with rotated elements, guides and images
embedded image, sheet, vector and web frames
a simulated slow worker and delayed hit-test response

gates.name: Safety
gates.criterion: all cancel, rollback, document replacement, permission, and cross-document async tests pass.

gates.name: Core input
gates.criterion: mouse selection, drag, marquee, resize, rotate, keyboard navigation, focus, text composition, and predictable Escape pass.

gates.name: Module conformance
gates.criterion: each first-party module passes context entry, focus, role, cancel/commit, and common inspector/shortcut checks.

gates.name: Visual/performance
gates.criterion: overlays align at supported DPR/zoom and camera states; pinned perf suite establishes acceptable budgets and no regression.

gates.name: Release
gates.criterion: browser matrix, accessibility manual tests, and critical crash/recovery scenarios pass. All documented exceptions include issue links, owner, severity, and an expiry/review date.

layers.name: Unit/property tests
layers.evidence: Pure hit/coordinate/math, modifier semantics, owner precedence, state transitions, cursor priority.

layers.name: Shell component tests
layers.evidence: Focus ownership, keyboard yield, inspector mixed states, menus, dialogs, context stack, error messages.

layers.name: WASM/engine channel
layers.evidence: Begin/update/commit/cancel, atomic mutation, permission refusal, replay/undo/redo.

layers.name: Browser journey (CPU)
layers.evidence: Real pointer/keyboard/IME behavior, panel/camera synchronization, document lifecycle.

layers.name: Browser journey (GPU)
layers.evidence: Same semantic outcomes, no overlay-render divergence, real-Chrome focus behavior.

layers.name: Visual regression
layers.evidence: Handles/snap/selection/preview alignment across zoom, DPR, themes, rotation.

layers.name: Accessibility manual
layers.evidence: Screen-reader journeys, keyboard-only tasks, touch/pen tasks, international input.

layers.name: Chaos/stress
layers.evidence: Delayed/reordered worker replies, blur, capture loss, doc switch, worker restart, large files.

requirements.title: At most one owner processes a pointer sequence; no simultaneous pan/marquee/transform.
Every started gesture terminates exactly once as committed, canceled, or failed and rolled back.
A canceled gesture leaves the document bitwise/semantically unchanged to the degree the engine's transaction contract promises; any rollback imperfection is a correctness defect.
A completed single gesture produces one undoable logical document change or none (e.g., selection/pan).
A stale asynchronous answer cannot overwrite a newer selection, document, context, or active gesture.
Screen-space handles, slop thresholds, snap acquisition, and hit targets are stable across zoom and device-pixel ratio.
Keyboard events belonging to an input, dialog, menu, IME, or plugin frame surface are not treated as canvas commands.
Changes initiated by panel, gesture, scripting, or plugin use the same authoritative mutation/permission boundary.
When a context changes or a panel opens, user selection and the intended canvas anchor remain stable except when navigation is explicitly requested.
A save-state label reflects what has actually been persisted and where.
An operation denied by permissions or unsupported capabilities has no document side effects and receives an actionable response.
Rendering, overlay, and accessibility representations must eventually converge on the same accepted selection/document revision.
The editor never consumes characters or keys used by in-progress input-method composition.
Pointer capture loss, OS window blur, document close, and unrecoverable worker failure cannot leave a gesture logically active.
No operation committed under a document/context revision may be accidentally applied to a subsequently opened document.
The host SHOULD expose a framework-independent coordinator responsible for event arbitration, gesture ownership, transition sequencing, and cancellation.
A session MUST only transition through legal edges.
Focus changes, tool changes, document replacement, and entering a modal MUST consult the coordinator before changing ownership.
A pointer gesture in progress MUST NOT become a text-edit gesture halfway through merely because hover changes.
Dispatch all canvas input through one arbitration decision.
A pointer capture belongs to the interaction session.
preventDefault() and stopPropagation() MUST be used only where the editor has explicitly claimed the event; avoid globally suppressing browser shortcuts or form behavior.
Nested plugin surfaces MUST be able to own their own events, but MUST provide a clear host return/exit path and MUST respect the document's role/permission policy.
Multiple editors embedded on one page MUST be isolated.
If determining a hit needs a worker request, record the pointer-down coordinates, viewport/camera transform, document/context epochs, modifiers, and interaction ID at the time of the request.
If movement begins before the hit resolves, buffer only the minimum latest pointer state necessary and resolve the eventual gesture against the original pointer-down geometry.
A late hit-test result is discarded when any epoch/token no longer matches.
Pointer capture loss while waiting for hit test ends the attempt without mutation.
Holding Space may temporarily engage Hand where the keyboard is owned by the canvas and no IME/composing input is active.
TARGET CHANGE / explicit policy choice: If a document-mutating gesture is already active, a temporary Hand override MUST NOT steal that pointer or commit/cancel the underlying edit.
A permanent tool switch during an active edit gesture MUST cancel it by default; a tool that expressly supports finish-on-switch needs a named exception and tests.
Camera and page/frame transforms MUST be inverted using a shared, tested transform utility.
When camera rotation is supported, hit tests, overlays, zoom anchors, page bounds, and drag deltas MUST use the full affine transform rather than an unrotated scale/translation shortcut.
A viewport resized or moved by opening panels MUST update both worker render dimensions and overlay coordinates before accepting new pointer input.
Pointer pressure, tilt, pointer type, and pen button are passed through when relevant, without changing mouse semantics.
Final numbers MUST be calibrated in user studies and per-input tests.
Explicit control handles and active edit-context handles take priority over page-item hit testing.
Among overlapping page items, resolve by visible stacking order and edit-context scope.
A transparent frame may still be selectable at its border; make the distinction between frame border hit and content hit discoverable.
Pasteboard objects use the same selection rules as page items where supported.
In nested contexts, out-of-scope clicks trigger defined context-exit/retarget logic, never an unguarded mutation of an outside object.
A future object-picker/cycle-selection affordance MAY expose the ordered stack beneath the pointer, but MUST not alter the default topmost-hit rule without explicit user input.
Object selection, text selection, path-point selection, and module-specific selection MUST be separate typed states.
Selection changes SHOULD be non-document operations (do not add to document undo history) unless a module has a documented, intentional alternative.
Selecting an object MUST update visible selection chrome, Properties, action applicability, and accessible selection state from the same accepted selection revision.
A drag on an unselected object's movable interior MUST move the object without requiring an initial selection click.
A drag that began on empty space remains a marquee even if the pointer crosses objects during movement.
The selection must not flicker between a stale and a newly requested set during asynchronous hit testing.

Copy/duplicate/move of a multi-selection preserves relative geometry and all eligible members; operations blocked for part of the set use an explicit all-or-none or subset policy (documented per action), never an…
Adopt a documented marquee-direction convention (recommended: left-to-right = fully contained; right-to-left = intersecting), visually distinguish both, and apply consistently across mouse and pen.
Invisible/locked/out-of-context objects follow the same selection eligibility rules as clicks.
The marquee rectangle is an overlay only; moving the pointer during selection never mutates geometry.
Default click targets a group's top-level selectable object according to the current context.
Double-click, Direct Selection, or an explicit drill-down affordance lets users target a nested object; the editor MUST show group ancestry or context scope.
Repeated drill-down cannot leave the user in an invisible editing scope.
Selecting a child in a group MUST NOT implicitly detach it, regroup the parent, or change stacking order.
Deleting a group versus deleting a child must be visually and semantically distinguishable before commit.
Inspector fields show mixed for differing values, never arbitrary first-item values represented as shared truth.
Multi-edit commits one logical operation over the intended eligible set.
Align/distribute acts on the selected set with explicit reference options (selection, key object, page, spread where supported), and preview should reflect that reference.
Every mutating gesture has the sequence:
The preview path MAY render imperatively, but persistent changes MUST go only through the engine mutation/gesture protocol.
A gesture MUST be cancelable from pointer down until its final operation has become irrevocably accepted.
The UI MUST NOT apply a document change simply by moving a DOM/SVG handle or by mutating an editor-side mirror of object geometry.
A successful single-object or multi-object drag results in exactly one logical undo step, including duplicate-drag and constrained transforms.
Cancel leaves no hidden cloned object, modified path, ghost guide, pending transaction, selection artifact, or stale status.
Terminalization MUST be idempotent: duplicate pointer-up / blur / cancel messages cannot cause a second mutation or a second cancellation error.
A gesture's resolved output SHOULD be a pure function of the gesture's initial model snapshot, current pointer position, and current normalized modifiers.
Modifiers MAY be fixed at gesture begin only if the interaction explicitly documents that semantic.
Shift during move constrains axis; Shift during resize preserves proportions when applicable; modifier precedence with Alt/Option for resize-from-center must be deterministic and visible.
Modifier transitions cannot result in geometry jumps unrelated to the pointer's anchor; recompute from initial snapshot rather than accumulating rounding error.
The coordinator MUST prevent a conflicting panel/script/plugin mutation from interleaving inside an active engine gesture.
Programmatic mutation APIs MUST be routed through the same operation ordering and permission checks as user gestures.
If a command is invoked while an edit gesture is active, it may not silently operate on a half-previewed geometry state.
During an active gesture the user sees correct cursor, drag/shape preview, selected bounds, and relevant modifiers; snapping and dimensions display only when useful.
On successful commit, transient preview disappears in coordination with authoritative render, without a visible double-flash or object jump.
On failed commit, show what failed and whether any change was applied.
Moving starts from an object's movable interior; dragging a control handle MUST NOT be interpreted as movement.
Selected sets move as a rigid arrangement unless the active transform explicitly acts on individual objects.
Resize preview must correspond to the selected handle, active transform origin, locked aspect ratio, and modifiers.
Rotation can be initiated through a recognized outside-corner zone (recommended), explicit rotate tool, or property field.
For rotated or sheared objects, drag geometry is computed in the intended object/page coordinate space.
Locked items cannot be transformed.
The cursor, preview, and actual committed result MUST agree on whether drag is move, copy, constrained move, scale, rotate, shear, crop, or content reposition.
Visual handles MAY be visually small, but target regions MUST be large enough for accurate mouse/stylus use and independent of zoom/DPR.
When hit regions overlap, prioritize the closer explicit handle with a stable deterministic tie-breaker; avoid a hover cursor changing rapidly between two actions.
Handles SHOULD be hidden or simplified at zoom levels too low to make geometry meaningful, while retaining keyboard/property access to the operation.
Rotation zones outside corners MUST not conflict with other page-item hits without a clear priority rule.
Snapping follows a clear hierarchy: explicit guide/grid and page margin references as configured; relevant object edges/centers/baselines; equal spacing; otherwise no snap.
A snap candidate MUST identify its target type in visual feedback, e.g., page center, guide, object edge, text baseline, or equal gap.
Snap acquisition and release thresholds are screen-space and use hysteresis to prevent flicker.
When multiple candidates are within tolerance, ranking MUST be deterministic for the same document/camera/pointer position.
Temporary snapping bypass MUST be consistent and documented (modifier assignment to be decided with the existing shortcut map).
Snap line/label MUST follow the same camera transform as document content and MUST clear on commit, cancel, context change, and renderer reset.
Snap feedback must not imply a constraint is permanently stored unless the operation actually creates such a relationship.
Starting a shape/path tool creates only a preview until its defined completion event; cancellation leaves no incomplete object.
A drawing tool that supports repeated creation SHOULD remain active after successful creation.
A Pen/path tool MUST distinguish path-start, continue, close, join, drag-handle, and finish states with appropriate cursor and hover feedback.

Escape behavior for multi-stage path creation SHOULD be progressive: cancel current uncommitted segment, or finish/cancel active path according to an explicit per-tool state; it MUST never silently delete previously…
Direct path editing MUST distinguish anchor points, Bézier handles, and segments.
All path edits that conceptually form one gesture MUST undo as one step.
Guide drag owns its pointer from ruler/guide hit; it cannot initiate a page marquee or object transform.
Creating, moving, or deleting a guide uses visible preview and one undo step for a document-stored guide.
Distinguish document guides from nonprinting structural aids (margins, bleed, grids).
Guide visibility and snap enablement are independent unless the product explicitly chooses otherwise; invisible guides must not unexpectedly pull geometry without an indication.
A text frame has at least two distinct selections: its containing page item and a caret/range within a story.
The UI MUST clearly transition between frame selection and text editing through tool choice, double-click, or explicit Edit text action.
Text editing inside a threaded story operates on story offsets, not arbitrary DOM text proxies, while showing caret/selection at the corresponding rendered location.
Text input MUST NOT be lost because a document render/worker message completes out of order.
Use a real accessible text-input surface capable of compositionstart, compositionupdate, compositionend, beforeinput, selection, and dead-key behavior.
While IME composition is active, canvas shortcuts (including Escape, Enter, arrow keys, Space, and tool letters) MUST yield to the input method.
Do not double-insert composition text by handling both compositionend and a resulting input event without reconciliation.

The composing string and candidate window should appear near the actual caret, and the input surface must be positioned in viewport coordinates accounting for page position, camera transform, and scroll.
AltGr, dead-key diacritics, right-to-left text, and mixed-direction text MUST be tested as user input, not treated as generic editor modifier chords.
Arrow/Home/End/Page keys within an active text-editing surface move the caret or selection according to text semantics and platform convention; they MUST NOT pan the document or nudge an object.
Drag selection, Shift + arrows, and range extension must preserve story order across line wraps and threaded frames.
If the engine answers a caret-navigation request asynchronously, later navigation requests MUST supersede stale answers without caret jumps.
The selection overlay, input surface, and actual model insertion point converge after every accepted edit.
Overset text indicators are actionable: users can identify the affected frame/story and navigate to it without permanently changing the document.
Text insertion/deletion goes through the same engine-authoritative mutation channel as other edits.
A text formatting operation on a selection MUST apply to the intended character/paragraph range, with mixed-style state represented accurately.
Undo/redo after insertion restores the same story content and an intelligible caret/selection position.
When the active frame disappears or becomes non-editable during a pending text write, reject/rollback and show a safe explanation.
Text out-port activation creates a distinct loaded-thread state and cursor.
Thread connection previews show source and destination clearly.
Invalid targets must be visually identified before click if possible; failed threading must leave both frames unchanged.
Edit contexts form a stack, not an unrelated mode toggle.
Entering the same context on the same root when it is already topmost is idempotent.
The editor MUST expose active context and a back path.
toolIds: null (no restriction declared) and toolIds: [] (no tools permitted) retain distinct meanings.
A context's user-facing label MUST describe the content, not only the internal plugin kind or registry ID.
CURRENT distinction: The checked-in EditContextStack exposes commit(), cancel(), pop(), exitAll({commit}), and isActiveDirty().
A dirty edit-context cancel should restore the context's pre-entry/pending state where supported, not rewrite previously saved document history.
Entering a context SHOULD change the tool/control rail and inspector without moving the page or resizing the canvas unnecessarily.
If the editor intentionally zooms to edit content, that is a separate, visible navigation action; preserve previous camera state and support return.
The host MUST prevent ordinary pointer selection outside an active context's declared selection scope.
CURRENT limitation: reviewed isInScope() recognizes the entered root element itself; general descendant membership is documented as future work.
Plugin edit contexts cannot bypass role policy.
Module authors must explicitly document if double-click opens a different context than the table recommends.
Keyboard ownership follows the focused UI element before canvas-wide handlers.

A native text field, select, contentEditable widget, or plugin-owned frame surface receives the keys required for its own editing, including Backspace, Delete, arrows, Home/End, Enter, Space, and text characters.
Dialogs, menus, comboboxes, trees, grids, tablists, sliders, and other ARIA composites own their appropriate navigation and activation keys.
A canvas-wide key listener MUST check composition state, defaultPrevented, active modal/menu ownership, and focused target before dispatching.
Plain tool shortcuts (e.g., V, T, P) apply only when the canvas/editor owns the key; never while typing in a text field or during IME composition.
Shortcuts shown in tooltips, menus, palette, and help MUST be derived from the actual active keybinding registry and reflect platform and profile scope.
Inactive, hidden, or disallowed module commands MUST NOT steal keybindings from the active context.
Pointer activation of a canvas editing action may focus the viewport when needed, but must not steal focus from a nested text editor, plugin surface, dialog, or focused field.
Opening a dialog/menu/palette moves focus into that surface; closing it restores focus to the invoking control or relevant canvas surface, provided the target still exists.
Pointer-based focus restoration MUST NOT unintentionally mark a keyboard-focused viewport as a pointer-engaged shortcut surface.
Each editor instance tracks its own focus ownership; an embedded editor must not receive shortcuts when the host page or another editor instance has focus.
An unhandled shortcut SHOULD fall through to the next eligible owner only if safe; a rejected command must not accidentally trigger a destructive fallback.
Primary means Meta on macOS and Ctrl where conventional elsewhere; localized keyboard layout and AltGr must be handled intentionally.
Hints must represent physical-versus-logical key semantics accurately (especially punctuation and non-US layouts).
A shortcut customization system MAY be introduced, but MUST make conflict and context scope visible and preserve recoverable defaults.
Escape resolution
Enter resolution
Tab resolution
Backspace/Delete resolution
Pan, zoom, and viewport resize do not change document geometry or history.
Zoom around a pointer preserves the document point under that pointer to within numerical/render rounding tolerance.
When panel layout changes, retain a meaningful camera anchor (viewport center, active caret, or explicitly selected target) instead of unexpectedly re-fitting the entire document.
A camera animation is interruptible.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion: navigation may jump immediately or use minimal motion without losing final location.
Camera bounds should prevent unusable lost-document states while allowing intentional pasteboard travel and precision work.
Every zoom route uses one common min/max range and camera transform semantics.
Opening a multi-page document defaults to a useful first-page fit (unless a saved view/restoration applies), not an unintelligible 4% fit of the whole document.
Fit commands must account for rotated canvas state where enabled.
Ordinary wheel or trackpad vertical scroll pans vertically over the viewport unless actively owned by a nested scrollable surface.
Middle-button or Space+drag pans while the canvas owns the pointer.
Two-finger touch pinch/translation uses a stable centroid anchor and doesn't emit object mutation.
One-finger touch behavior depends on the current profile and edit context.
PageUp/PageDown/Home/End and thumbnail clicks must respect focus ownership.
The current page indicator identifies the page corresponding to the viewport's meaningful focus/center with documented tie-breaking, not a random page from a stale render.

Clicking a preflight issue, search result, comment, link, or structure entry may navigate and select, but MUST preserve a navigable return path (view history preferred) and distinguish selection from document mutation.
At very low zoom, hide or simplify tiny ruler labels, point handles, and other unreadable overlays while preserving page names, highlights, and navigation.
The worker owns document pixels; the main thread owns interaction overlays.
Overlay stacking order is defined, not accidental CSS z-index history.
Hidden overlays must not capture pointers or keyboard focus.
Every overlay with interactive handles declares accessible action names and touch/pointer target sizes.
Overlay geometry must account for camera rotation and page position, and updates must not lag one stale camera revision after pan/zoom.
Hover indication is lighter than selection indication; hover does not silently change selection.
Selection outlines, anchors, and resize handles must remain visible over varied page colors in light and dark chrome (consider dual-stroke or contrast halo rather than a single thin color).
Locked/noneditable and mixed selections are visually distinguishable with shape/icon/label, not color alone.
Context-appropriate object labels MAY appear on hover but should not obscure text and must not be relied on as the only accessible description.
Cursor state MUST derive from current hover target + effective tool + active context + gesture phase; do not hard-code it independently in multiple components.

Use progressive feedback levels: inline validation near a field, nonblocking toast for brief operation result, persistent Problems/Health entry for unresolved document issues, blocking dialog only for high-risk…
An error message SHOULD contain: attempted action, reason, whether the document changed, and next remedy.
Success messages should be subtle for common continuous edits, prominent for Save/Export/Import/long-running operations where confirmation matters.
Progress language must distinguish measurable percent from unknown-duration stage.
The canvas should visually signal file drop intent (Place image, Replace contents, Open document) before release; disabled or unsupported targets explain what is not possible.
Context transitions and overlay animations must be interruptible, short, and optional under reduced-motion settings.
No essential state is conveyed only by motion.
The default Properties inspector reflects the active typed selection or edit context.
Common properties use the same unit/rounding/input, mixed-value, reset, validation, and undo semantics across host and plugin panels.
If a property is unavailable, communicate whether it is inapplicable to current selection, read-only due to permissions, unsupported by the engine, or temporarily unavailable due to loading.
A disabled control must not look enabled.

Inspector fields commit according to explicit input type: numeric scrub as one undo step, text field on Enter/blur where appropriate, color chooser on apply/accepted change, and Escape returns pre-edit value if…
Panel actions triggered during a canvas gesture MUST wait for safe ownership resolution and cannot operate on speculative geometry.
Opening, resizing, pinning, or hiding panels should preserve canvas anchor and active edit context.
Fields display Mixed if selected objects differ; empty and zero are separate states.
Numeric property inputs MAY support expressions (e.g., 10 mm + 2 pt) once validated; calculation results and unit conversion must be deterministic.
Bulk edits clearly state their scope and apply in a single coherent undo step.
Data-bound fields visibly indicate binding and source; changing a value cannot silently break a binding unless the action explicitly requests it.
Menus, palette, context menus, toolbar buttons, keyboard shortcuts, and scripts resolve through the same command/applicability model where they represent the same user operation.
Applicability is derived from active document, selection, edit context, role/permissions, feature gates, and module capabilities.
A command that fails MUST surface a user-readable error with no misleading success status.
A successful command SHOULD restore focus to a meaningful canvas or original control, unless it intentionally enters a new field/dialog/context.
A command palette item with a name and shortcut MUST execute the same underlying command as the corresponding menu item.
Keyboard navigation, typeahead, Escape dismissal, and focus restoration of the palette are tested in bundled Chromium and real Chrome, both CPU and GPU lanes where available.
Right-click/secondary click resolves selection under the pointer before constructing an object-specific menu where feasible.
Right-click empty canvas must not automatically discard selection unless that behavior is an explicitly adopted policy; menu actions should make their target clear.
Shift+F10 and the Context Menu key open the relevant menu at a useful anchored point near focused selection or viewport center, not offscreen.
Context menu opening and dismissal must be available without a mouse, honor focus priority, and not trigger the underlying canvas action twice.
Determine drop intent from file MIME/format, source, pointer target, current selection/context, and active role.
During drag-over, show a clearly named drop target and pending effect; cursor and label match the action that will happen if released.
Document replacement always passes through the same unsaved-change guard, independent of whether invoked by File menu, command palette, drag-and-drop, automation, or host action.
Drop handling must not steal a live pointer gesture or apply to a document that changed between drag-over and drop; revalidate document/context epoch on release.
Copy, Cut, Paste, Duplicate and Paste in Place operate on active selection type and context with clear fallback rules.
Cut is atomic: content is not deleted unless clipboard write (where required) and document mutation succeed as a coherent action, or failure is safely handled without data loss.
Object paste preserves supported appearance and resource references, with a documented target positioning policy.
Clipboard serialization includes enough information to distinguish native Paged objects, rich text, images, and plain text.
When pasting into another document or module, revalidate permissions and compatibility, and never inadvertently overwrite source content.
Loading an unsupported/corrupt file must not replace the current document with a misleading success state.
Imports that convert unsupported features SHOULD offer a readable import/loss report with affected objects or pages where possible; technical codes may be available in an expandable detail view.
Save/export state distinguishes saving, saved locally, synced remotely, failed, and unsaved edits, only when those persistence guarantees are true.
Export standards and output options are validated before starting.
Export progress is cancellable where the engine supports cancellation; completion must identify output location and warnings, and never present an unverified artifact as successful.
Every document change initiated by a panel, tool, module, script, AI-assisted workflow, keyboard command, or plugin goes through authorized engine operation/mutation interfaces.
Operations carry sufficient document identity and transaction context to reject changes intended for a previous document or invalidated selection scope.
Engine role/document policy is checked regardless of UI visibility.
Command and script automation use the same undo/redo model as GUI actions; the UI does not label a workflow reversible unless it can restore the appropriate model state.
Undo returns a committed operation to its precise pre-state; redo returns it to post-state without duplicating assets or shifting frames.
Preview state must never become an extra history item.
Undo/redo while an uncommitted gesture or dirty nested context exists must first resolve that active interaction; do not interleave two models of history.
Dirty state reflects accepted document changes not yet persisted to the declared save target.
A local journal/checkpoint must not be presented as confirmed remote sync.
Crash/session recovery should distinguish recoverable local state, last explicit saved state, and remote canonical state; selecting recovery must not silently overwrite source content.
Save guards apply before destructive document replacement and after dirty nested contexts are safely resolved.
Scripts that mutate content must be ordered relative to active gestures and panel changes; they cannot be applied between gesture preview and commit arbitrarily.
A recorded user workflow should record semantic commands and object references/selection intent, not raw viewport pixel coordinates whenever possible.
Replay validates document, context, permissions, and available capabilities; if assumptions do not hold, the user receives a precise refusal rather than silently targeting another object.
Each async UI request affecting document, selection, focus, context, cursor, or overlay must be correlated with a request/session token and document/context epoch.
A response to an obsolete epoch MUST be ignored.
A new gesture supersedes stale selection geometry requests that would otherwise apply old handles or incorrect inspector values.
Resizing the viewport during a worker render may temporarily display old pixels; overlays must not claim exact alignment to a mismatched frame.
If the render worker becomes unavailable, block unsafe mutations and show a bounded recovery state.
A worker restart must not accidentally double-submit previously accepted operations.
Render fallback from WebGPU to CPU cannot change selection semantics, hit targets, or document output intent.
For every race case, success means one coherent result, no cross-document mutation, no orphaned gesture, and no false save state.
Classify outcomes as success, canceled, blocked, unsupported, invalid-input, conflict/stale, recoverable-failure, or fatal-failure for UI response purposes.
The affected control should show an inline error if local; global document failures go to a persistent Problems/Health source.
Errors contain no raw stack trace or opaque internal IDs by default; developer diagnostics may expose a correlation ID and technical detail.
Menus, dialogs, tablists, tree views, panels, command palette, and controls use appropriate ARIA roles/states and native focus semantics.
Users can reach the canvas from keyboard and leave it without pointer assistance.
Selection and object actions have accessible names, type, state, and relationships.
When an object is selected through the accessibility tree, the canvas selection and inspector reflect the same object ID.
Dialog opens place focus inside; dialog close restores focus.
All essential document editing actions have an available keyboard command, accessible menu/control, or equivalent non-pointer flow.
Object position and size may be edited precisely through inspector fields; selected objects may be nudged with arrow keys when canvas owns keys.
Keyboard selection of overlapping/nested objects must be possible through a structure/layers view or explicit selection cycle.
Touch targets and hit zones meet practical size/spacing guidance.
Pen pressure/tilt affect only tools that declare support; selection, navigation, and inspector editing remain usable with pen.
In viewer/form/template-fill profiles on narrow touch screens, navigation and field entry take priority over dense desktop chrome, in line with existing compact profile behavior.
Status and errors use text/icon as well as color; relevant text and control contrast must satisfy the product's WCAG target (recommend WCAG 2.2 AA as adoption baseline).
Reduced motion applies to camera, panel, and overlay transitions.
Locale changes affect labels, shortcut hints where appropriate, numeric/length parsing conventions, and status text without changing underlying document geometry.
Bidirectional text, CJK IME, dead keys, and screen-reader focus are release-gated by cross-browser tests, not treated as post-release polish.
The editor MUST prioritize continuity of pointer and keyboard interaction over eagerly rendering invisible pages.
During expensive live operations, a temporary reduced-resolution preview MAY be used if placement/geometry remains correct and it is never mistaken for final output fidelity.
Loading stages should expose recognized document, page geometry, first useful paint, and background refinement, without invented percent complete.
Page thumbnails, tile caches, decoded assets, fonts, and history snapshots need explicit memory budgets and eviction rules to prevent unbounded growth.
Active viewport and nearby pages receive priority over distant pages; stale render requests should be discarded if the camera moves.
Automated perf suites measure end-to-end perceptual outcome (input → worker/model acknowledgment → visible frame) separately from main-thread React latency.
Performance defects that change interaction semantics (lost pointer, stale selection, dropped text, partial mutation) are correctness blockers, not merely perf regressions.
Every tool contribution declares the pointer/keyboard events it handles and how it cancels or commits.
Every edit-context contribution declares entry trigger, active tool restrictions, panel emphasis, content pointer handling, dirty/commit/cancel semantics, and scope boundary as applicable.
Plugin native controls inside panels use the host's theme, focus, disabled, error, and shortcut semantics.
Plugin commands, panels, and tools participate in the same applicability and feature gates as host contributions.
Plugin failures cannot leave the canvas gesture owner, focus, or edit-context stack inconsistent.
Plugin context scope is not a security barrier; the engine checks permissions for all operations.
Removing a visible UI control through a profile MUST NOT be treated as sufficient authorization.
Changing profiles at runtime must resolve active gesture and content context safely, restore meaningful focus, and never lose uncommitted work without confirmation.

A development-only interaction trace SHOULD record timestamp, editor scope, document epoch, interaction ID, owner, tool, phase, input device, relevant coordinates without user text content, result, and latency.
The trace must not capture raw story text, document bytes, secret tokens, or personally identifying content.
Each unexpected transition should provide an actionable development diagnostic, e.g., stale hit-test discarded, gesture canceled: capture lost, context rejected: scope mismatch.
Production logging, if later introduced, requires separate privacy/security review; this spec does not authorize telemetry upload.
For each migrated tool, compare observable model/undo/render outcomes to prior behavior except where an approved TARGET CHANGE deliberately alters it.
No legacy key handler remains active in parallel with a new owner for the same event class; CI should assert no duplicate callbacks/operations.
Use feature gates for risky input routing transitions, but keep user-visible behavior consistent across gate variants whenever possible.
Keep one list of exceptions with planned retirement.

tests.title: Click an unselected rectangle
tests.assertion: Only that object selected; inspector and accessibility tree agree.

tests.title: Drag an unselected rectangle
tests.assertion: Object moves in same gesture; no marquee; one undo step.

tests.title: Drag empty page across items
tests.assertion: Marquee, no objects moved; selection follows direction policy.

tests.title: Shift-click three items, toggle one off
tests.assertion: Set membership correct, no duplicate IDs.

tests.title: Drag one of three selected objects
tests.assertion: All eligible items move together; relative offsets unchanged.

interactions.title: Selection and Direct Selection: a click selects what is under the pointer
interactions.permission: Selection is not a document change; the worker's hit test picks the target and a locked item stays selectable (ADR 251).
interactions.cancel: A release under the click threshold settles; the hit-test answer carries no epoch, so a late one can apply (IC3).
interactions.notes: Shift adds and Cmd toggles today (ADR 235); ADR 1201 makes Shift toggle (D-01).

interactions.title: Selection: a drag that starts on empty canvas draws a marquee
interactions.permission: No document change; the marquee takes what it intersects, page by page (EN2 adds contain/intersect, scope and the pasteboard).
interactions.cancel: pointercancel and window blur abort it; Escape does not cancel a marquee yet (IC2).

interactions.title: Selection: a drag on an object moves the selection (Alt duplicates)
interactions.permission: One engine translate gesture; the engine refuses a locked item.
interactions.cancel: Escape cancels the engine gesture and the rest of the drag pans; pointercancel and window blur abort; lostpointercapture and unmount do not yet, and an orphaned gesture turns later drags into pans (IC2).

interactions.title: Selection: a resize or rotate handle drag transforms the selection
interactions.permission: Bounds resize, matrix scale or rotation as one engine gesture; the engine refuses a locked item.
interactions.cancel: As the move: Escape cancels and the drag pans on; pointercancel and blur abort (IC2).
interactions.notes: ViewportCanvas reads the handle under the press (readHandleAttr) and begins the gesture; resize cursors ignore rotation (IC7).

interactions.title: Selection: a bundle's overlay handle (a preset's adjust handle) drags its parameter
interactions.permission: The bundle's handle router commits through the engine; it wins over the path session, the resize handles, the move and the marquee (extensions ADR 1103).
interactions.cancel: Escape calls the router's cancel (ViewportCanvas onEscapeKey).

interactions.title: Direct Selection: path-edit mode drags anchors, handles and its anchor marquee
interactions.permission: Path edits are engine operations over paged.draw's machine.
interactions.cancel: Escape mid-drag undoes the drag and keeps the mode; Escape idle leaves the mode (usePathEditMode's own listener).

interactions.title: Type: a click places a text caret
interactions.permission: Placing a caret is not a document change.
interactions.cancel: Settles on release; nothing to roll back.
interactions.notes: The press arms the Type gesture handler too (ViewportCanvas legacyAlso); the release splits click from drag at CLICK_DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX.

interactions.title: Type: a drag draws a text frame
interactions.permission: One engine operation on commit; the engine refuses an edit the document's role or a lock forbids.
interactions.cancel: Escape reaches the handler through the gesture spine's key path (useGestureSpine) unless canvasKeyYields; pointercancel and window blur end the drag; lostpointercapture and unmount do not yet (IC2).

interactions.title: Double-click enters the hit frame's content: a story caret, a group level or a module context
interactions.permission: Entering a context changes no document state; the context's write scope is its root plus what the engine's scope query answers (editor ADR 1211; the root alone until EN5 reaches the client, UXI-CTX-011).
interactions.cancel: Nothing to cancel on entry; the hit test that picks the target carries no epoch (IC3).
interactions.notes: A picture frame enters its content level first and Edit image on a second double-click, Enter or the level control (D-05, editor ADR 1212); tryEnterEditContext decides every double-click, picture frames included. Stays legacy until track IC's ContentContextAdapter routes the canvas's double-click through it.

interactions.title: An edit context that opts into content pointers takes presses over its frame
interactions.permission: The module answers in content coordinates and writes through its own engine operations.
interactions.cancel: The module's own; nothing coordinates it with the canvas Escape listeners (KF1).

interactions.title: A press outside an edit context's frame leaves the context through the exit resolver, then selects
interactions.permission: Leaves through resolveContextExit (editor ADR 1211): a clean context commits at once; a dirty one commits when its module declares commit-if-safe, asks (Keep / Discard / Cancel) when it declares ask.
interactions.cancel: An open resolve prompt holds the press (Cancel keeps the context); otherwise the press falls through to select what is under it (D-04).
interactions.notes: The resolver and useContextExit are in the shell; the canvas switches its commit() to leave("click-outside") with track IC (ViewportCanvas.tsx is IC's).

interactions.title: Hand: a drag pans the view
interactions.permission: Camera only; no document change.
interactions.cancel: Release ends it; nothing to roll back.

interactions.title: Holding Space engages Hand until it is released
interactions.permission: Tool override only; no document change. Yields to a focused control and to a live text caret.
interactions.cancel: Key-up pops the override; window blur clears every override.
interactions.notes: A press during a mutating drag swaps the gesture spine's single handler slot; ADR 1201 defers it until the drag settles (D-09).

interactions.title: Holding Cmd engages Direct Selection until it is released
interactions.permission: Tool override only; no document change. A tool that reads Cmd as a gesture modifier keeps it (Free Transform).
interactions.cancel: Key-up pops the override; window blur clears every override.

interactions.title: Zoom: a click zooms in, Alt-click zooms out
interactions.permission: Camera only; no document change.
interactions.cancel: Settles on release.

interactions.title: Zoom: a drag pans (no rectangle zoom yet)
interactions.permission: Camera only; no document change.
interactions.cancel: Release ends it; nothing to roll back.

interactions.title: Holding Cmd+Space engages Zoom until it is released
interactions.permission: Tool override only; no document change.
interactions.cancel: Key-up pops the override; window blur clears every override.

interactions.title: The wheel pans; Cmd+wheel and the trackpad pinch zoom about the pointer
interactions.permission: Camera only; no document change.
interactions.cancel: Each event settles; an animation in flight can tug the camera back (WS8).

interactions.title: A middle-button drag pans, whatever the tool
interactions.permission: Camera only; no document change.
interactions.cancel: Release ends it; nothing to roll back.

interactions.title: A two-finger touch pinch zooms and pans
interactions.permission: Camera only; no document change.
interactions.cancel: Lifting the fingers ends it; a pending one-finger selection is not arbitrated against it yet (AP4).

interactions.title: Measure: a drag reads a distance and an angle
interactions.permission: Reads only; no document change.
interactions.cancel: Escape reaches the handler through the gesture spine's key path (useGestureSpine) unless canvasKeyYields; pointercancel and window blur end the drag; lostpointercapture and unmount do not yet (IC2).

interactions.title: A drag from a ruler or on a guide creates or moves a guide
interactions.permission: One guide operation on release; guides on a locked layer refuse.
interactions.cancel: Escape cancels through the controller's own window capture listener; window pointer listeners own the drag (IC4 makes it a session).

interactions.title: Clicking a text frame's out-port loads the cursor; the next click threads to the target
interactions.permission: One link operation; an invalid target refuses.
interactions.cancel: Escape and pointercancel unload the cursor through window capture listeners (IC4 makes it a session).

interactions.title: Place: a loaded place cursor puts the image where the user clicks or drags
interactions.permission: One place operation at the answered point; cancelling is an ordinary answer with nothing placed.
interactions.cancel: Escape answers nothing through a window capture listener; a stolen capture still answers with the press (IC4 makes it a session).

interactions.title: A file dropped on the canvas area goes to the app's file handler
interactions.permission: The app's handler opens, imports or places the first file by type; a document replacement asks the replace question (ADR 230).
interactions.cancel: Leaving the canvas or Escape during the drag ends it; no intent is shown before release (DF3).

interactions.title: A secondary click opens the canvas context menu for what is under the pointer
interactions.permission: Opening the menu changes no document state; each item runs its command through applicability.
interactions.cancel: Escape or a press outside closes the menu; the hit test that resolves its target carries no epoch (IC3).

interactions.title: Shift+F10 and the Context Menu key open the canvas context menu
interactions.permission: Opening the menu changes no document state.
interactions.cancel: Escape closes the menu and keeps the selection.

interactions.title: Cmd/Ctrl+\ toggles the chrome; Tab does on a clicked canvas only with "Tab hides panels (InDesign)" on
interactions.permission: Chrome only; no document change.
interactions.cancel: Pressing it again restores the chrome.
interactions.notes: ADR 1201 D-03 is built (KF3, ADR 234's amendment): Tab moves focus by default; paged.view.toggleChrome replaces paged.chrome.toggleAll (deprecated 0.78 to 0.80); the opt-in setting is stored under paged.keyboard.tabHidesPanels.

interactions.title: Cmd+K opens the command palette; Escape closes it and restores focus
interactions.permission: No document change; the palette runs commands through applicability.
interactions.cancel: The palette tier of the Escape arbiter (editor ADR 1207) closes it wherever focus is in the editor, whatever Radix layer is on top (issue #32); focus returns to the opener, else the canvas (ADR 1206).

interactions.title: Typing, composition and editing keys go to the active text caret
interactions.permission: Each accepted edit is one engine text operation; a story the role forbids refuses.
interactions.cancel: Composition is the input method's: a composition commits once per caret session (no echo from a trailing input event) and is dropped when the caret moved mid-composition (KF4).

interactions.title: Escape cancels the canvas move or handle drag
interactions.permission: Cancels or leaves without a document change of its own.
interactions.cancel: Cancels the engine gesture; the rest of the drag pans (IC2 stops the pan).

interactions.title: Escape reaches the active gesture handler
interactions.permission: Cancels or leaves without a document change of its own.
interactions.cancel: Forwarded to the handler unless canvasKeyYields; each handler cancels its own way.

interactions.title: Escape leaves text editing for the frame
interactions.permission: Cancels or leaves without a document change of its own.
interactions.cancel: The text tier of the Escape arbiter (editor ADR 1207): leaves the caret for the frame that held it, after a gesture, a transient mode and an edit context, before an entered group and the selection; never during a composition (the IME's).

interactions.title: Escape ends a path-edit drag, then the mode
interactions.permission: Cancels or leaves without a document change of its own.
interactions.cancel: Mid-drag undoes the drag; idle leaves path-edit mode.

interactions.title: Escape climbs out of the entered group
interactions.permission: Cancels or leaves without a document change of its own.
interactions.cancel: The group tier of the Escape arbiter (editor ADR 1207): climbs one level (ADR 250); answers only while the tool in hand has no gesture handler until track IC joins the gestures.

interactions.title: Escape leaves the active edit context through the exit resolver
interactions.permission: Cancels or leaves without a document change of its own.
interactions.cancel: The context tiers of the Escape arbiter (editor ADR 1207): a dirty sub-edit resolves through the context's onContentKey (or the tool in hand); a clean context leaves one level through resolveContextExit (editor ADR 1211: cancel, or commit for a commit-if-safe module); a header edited in place leaves its Escape to the text.

interactions.title: Escape cancels a guide drag
interactions.permission: Cancels or leaves without a document change of its own.
interactions.cancel: A transient mode of the Escape arbiter (editor ADR 1205): drops the live preview, nothing else answers the press.

interactions.title: Escape unloads the threading cursor
interactions.permission: Cancels or leaves without a document change of its own.
interactions.cancel: A transient mode of the Escape arbiter (editor ADR 1207): unloads the cursor, nothing else answers the press.

interactions.title: Escape cancels a pending placement
interactions.permission: Cancels or leaves without a document change of its own.
interactions.cancel: A transient mode of the Escape arbiter (editor ADR 1207): answers the placement with nothing, nothing else answers the press.

interactions.title: Escape at the top level clears the selection
interactions.permission: A selection change, not a document change and not an undo step (D-15).
interactions.cancel: The selection tier of the Escape arbiter (editor ADR 1207), the last one: clears the selection when nothing else answers; only while the tool in hand has no gesture handler until track IC joins the gestures.

exceptions.scope: Escape on the canvas while the viewport's drag cancel, the gesture handlers and path editing still listen on their own (they defer to the Escape arbiter, ADR 1207, until track IC registers them)
exceptions.why: Three listeners still answer Escape at the document and the editor root on their own conditions; the arbiter defers to them (a pointer held on the canvas, path editing), so their press is theirs alone, but nothing yet orders the viewport's cancel against the gesture spine's.
exceptions.repro: Begin a move with a drawing tool's handler in hand inside an entered group and press Escape: the handler and the viewport both see the key (the arbiter defers to the pointer held on the canvas).
